His brilliance lies not just in his dazzling scales but in his mind—sharp, calculating, and always three steps ahead. During the Battle of Duskwatch, Kalspire hovered silently above the fray, his keen eyes assessing the battlefield.  <style="Inline_H1">Region Ownership</style>
 Factions begin holding a region by conquering its <style="Inline_Bold">Seat of Power</style>. 

Holding a region provides strategic benefits, such as stronger defense and blocking enemy stronghold relocation.¬¬¯¯UI_TILESELECT_DEFENDER_TOOLTIP_TITLE¬¬Tile Defense Mechanics¬¬¯¯UI_TILESELECT_DEFENDER_TOOLTIP_DESCRIPTION¬¬<style="Inline_Overview">Every tile is protected by <style="Inline_Bold">Tile Defenders</style> and has a <style="Inline_Bold">Durability</style> amount.</style>

To conquer a tile, defeat all Tile Defenders first, then reduce it's Durability to 0.

- <b>Tile Defenders:</b> armies stationed on the tile
- <b>Durability</b>: the tile's siege health

<style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege Troops</style> deal the most damage to Durability. <style="Inline_H2">Limited Time</style>
Stages only last for a set time, so act quickly.

<style="Inline_H2">Rewards at the End</style>
Complete objectives now to claim your rewards when the stage ends.

<style="Inline_H2">Stage Effects</style>
Some stages include special effects or buffs that change how the game plays.

<style="Inline_H2">Story Progression</style>
At the end of each stage, a new part of the campaign story is revealed.

Plan ahead, stay flexible, and adapt as each new stage unfolds!¬¬¯¯CAMPAIGN_ENDING_INFOPANEL_HEADER¬¬Campaign Overview¬¬¯¯CAMPAIGN_ENDING_INFOPANEL_TEXT¬¬<style="Inline_Overview">Campaigns offer you a path into the heart of Westeros, playing through epic scenarios that shape the realm’s future. Each Campaign lasts a set time—usually 8 weeks.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">At the End of a Campaign:</style>
<style="Inline_H2">Progress Resets</style>
Your dragon levels, stronghold upgrades, tile ownership will reset. Basic resources, including unused resources, will expire.

<style="Inline_H2">Goal Rewards</style>
Complete Campaign Goals to earn <style="Inline_Bold">durable</style> rewards like Gold and Hatchery Keys that do not expire between campaigns, strengthening your dragon collection for future battles.

<style="Inline_Underline">Rewards can be claimed at the start of the next Campaign.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Types of Goals:</style>
<style="Inline_H2">Personal Goals </style>
Objectives you complete on your own.

<style="Inline_H2">Faction Goals</style>
Team-based objectives completed with your allies. <style="Inline_H1">Conquering Towns</style>

4. <style="Inline_Bold">Conquer</style> the tile

<style="Inline_H1">Garrison Benefits</style>
<style="Inline_Underline">Every faction member</style> can garrison a limited number of armies in a Town.

<indent=3%>- <style="Inline_Positive">Faster Marches:</style> Armies march faster when sent to a garrison.</indent>
<indent=3%>- <style="Inline_Positive">Rapid Reinforcement:</style> Armies reinforce faster while at the garrison.</indent>
<indent=3%>- <style="Inline_Positive">Recall Point:</style> Defeated or recalled armies that are garrisoned return to the Town—not your stronghold.</indent>

At Towns, you can also change troop types and adjust dragon lane assignments in your army.

Rills¬¬¯¯TILE_STALEMATE_INFO_MODAL_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Overview">If after 10 rounds of battle, neither army was able to defeat the other a <style="Inline_Bold">stalemate</style> occurs.

During a stalemate, attackers and defenders have different options:</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Attacker</style>
<indent=5%><style="Inline_Bold">Wait</style> — Allow the timer to expire and automatically attack again without spending additional stamina.</indent>
<indent=5%><style="Inline_Bold">Recall</style> — Withdraw your army from the tile to free them from the stalemate for reinforcing or other actions.</indent>
<indent=5%><style="Inline_Bold">Attack Again</style> — Send a different army to press the advantage against the weakened defender.</indent>

Lashed by salt wind and icy waves, it keeps vigil over the narrow sea and the frozen wilderness beyond.¬¬¯¯STAR_PROGRESSION_MAX_ARMY_BOOST¬¬Max Army Boost¬¬¯¯STAR_PROGRESSION_MAX_ARMY_BOOST_DESC¬¬Reach {0} Stars to unlock +{1}% additional troops to your army size.¬¬¯¯POI_SEATSOFPOWER_DESC¬¬<style="Inline_Overview">This is a <style="Inline_Bold">Seat of Power</style>, a key stronghold in the region serving as a center of influence.</style>



<style="Inline_H1">Faction Ownership</style>
When a faction conquers a <style="Inline_Bold">Seat of Power</style> they start holding the region, blocking enemy relocations and providing defensive bonuses to faction-owned tiles in the area.



Seats of Power are <u>heavily defended</u> with high Durability, requiring a well-coordinated attack with allies to conquer.

<style="Inline_H1">Point of Interest Bonuses</style>
Seats of Power are key progression targets. To maximize success, secure regional Castles and lower-level Seats of Power for the best chance at conquering higher-level seats.



<style="Inline_H1">Conquering a Seat of Power</style>
<style="Inline_H2">1. Secure Nearby Bases:</style> Conquer nearby Towns or Castles and use them as garrisons to quickly replenish troops.

<style="Inline_H2">2. Relocate Your Stronghold:</style> Move closer for faster reinforcements.

<style="Inline_H2">3. Coordinate the Attack:</style> Plan the attack with allies for greater impact.

<style="Inline_H2">4. Assemble Your Forces:</style> Gather at a connected tile with at least 1 army to combat the defenders and 1 siege army to reduce Durability.

<style="Inline_H2">5. <style="Inline_H1">Faction Ownership</style>
When a faction conquers a <style="Inline_Bold">Capital</style> they start holding the region, blocking enemy relocations and providing defensive bonuses to all faction-owned tiles in the area.

Capitals are <u>heavily defended</u> with high Durability, requiring a well-coordinated attack with allies to conquer.

<style="Inline_H1">Conquering a Capital</style>
<style="Inline_H2">1. Secure Nearby Bases:</style> Take control of nearby Towns or Castles and use them as garrisons to swiftly reinforce your troops.

<style="Inline_H2">2. Relocate Your Stronghold:</style> Move closer to the Capital to reduce travel time for reinforcements.

<style="Inline_H2">3. Coordinate the Attack:</style> Work closely with your allies to ensure maximum impact.

<style="Inline_H2">4. Assemble Your Forces:</style> Gather at a connected tile with at least one army to fight defenders and one siege army to reduce Durability.

<style="Inline_H2">5. Clear Defenders First:</style> Defeat all defending armies before deploying your siege forces.

<style="Inline_Bold">Encounters</style> are powerful enemies that appear on the map for a limited time. Defeat them with your armies to earn valuable rewards.

Hunting uses Resolve (a special energy that regenerates over time or can be refreshed daily for a <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style> cost), <style="inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>, or a combination of both depending on the type of Encounter.

<indent=3%><style="Inline_UnownedTile">Grey</style>: Unowned
<style="Inline_OwnedTile">Green</style>: Owned by you.
<style="Inline_AllianceTile">Blue</style>: Owned by someone in your alliance.
<style="Inline_FactionTile">Purple</style>: Owned by your faction allies. 
<style="Inline_RivalTile">Red</style>: Owned by enemy factions.</indent>

Choose a tab, select what you want, then tap <b>Search</b>. The Navigator searches a 100x100 area around your current camera position, jumps to the nearest match, and highlights it.
 
 <style="Inline_H1">Encounters</style>
 Locate <style="Inline_Bold">beast or human encounters</style> by selecting a <style="Inline_Bold">type</style> (e.g., Outlaws, Wildlings, Boars) and <style="Inline_Bold">level range</style>.
 
 To quickly target encounters that grant progress toward <style="Inline_Bold">active events</style>, toggle <style="Inline_Bold">Event Encounters</style> on. This highlights only the encounters that contribute to your current event objectives.
 
 <style="Inline_H1">Wild Dragons</style>
 Find <style="Inline_Bold">wild dragon encounters</style> by choosing a <style="Inline_Bold">breed</style> (Champion, Hunter, Sentinel, or Warrior) and a <style="Inline_Bold">level range</style>.
 
Wild Dragons are a primary source of <style="Inline_Bold">Breedmarks</style>, used to advance your dragons <style="Inline_Bold">Habits</style>. Each Breed of Wild Dragon drops a specific Breedmark and has a weakness to one other Breed.
 
 Bring an army with dragons of the <style="Inline_Bold">stronger Breed</style> when challenging a Wild Dragon. Exploiting these strengths will reduce your losses.
 
 <style="Inline_H1">Refreshing Results</style>
 Whenever your camera moves including when scrolling through results with the arrow buttons, the number on the Search button will update.
 
 <style="Inline_Bold">If it says Searching (0):</style> No results in view. Move your camera until the number changes.
 
 <style="Inline_Bold">If it says Update Search (#):</style> Tap to refresh and load those results.
 
 <style="Inline_H1">Finding More</style>
 Tap the left and right arrows to jump to the next closest match. The Navigator cycles through all nearby matches before returning to the first one.
 
 <style="Inline_H1">No Matches?</style>
 If nothing's found, move your camera to a new area and watch for the number on the Search button to update, then tap to search again.

<style="Inline_Title">How it Works</style>
<style="Inline_H1">1. Prep Phase (Before the Fight Starts)</style>
The prep phase consists of two sections:

<style="Inline_Bold">Troop Formation</style>
This section shows how both teams were set up at the beginning:
<indent=3%>- Troop Type and Troop Count for each dragon
- Where each dragon started (what lane they were in)
- Any Troop Advantage/Disadvantage and/or Affinity bonuses that were active at the start</indent>

<style="Inline_Bold">Preparations</style>
Any special global effects will be listed here, such as effects from City Upgrades, Boosts, etc.

<style="Inline_H1">2. Combat Phase (The Battle Itself)</style>
Every action in each round of the battle is listed here, in the order they happened.

For each action, you’ll see:
<indent=3%>- Who acted (dragon + team), and which lane they’re in
- Who they targeted, and their lane
- What move they used (like a Basic Attack or Command)
- Any special effects active at that moment</indent>

For active special effects, you'll see:
<indent=3%>- The name of the effect
- Who it’s on
- What it does

Example:
<i>[Thunderstrike] is under the effect of [Battle Rush] from itself. +20% Initiative.</i></indent>

For the results, you'll see:
<indent=3%>- Damage dealt
- Troops lost or gained
- If a move worked or failed
- If a dragon moved lanes, ran away, or if the battle ended

Example:
<i>[Antares] uses [Basic Attack] to attack [Outlaws] (Vanguard). Deals 7 Physical damage against [Outlaws].
[Outlaws] takes 7 losses (63 remaining).</i></indent>

<style="Inline_H2">How to Hunt: Group Encounters</style>
This is a type of <style="Inline_Bold">Group Encounter</style>. Group Encounters are powerful enemies designed to challenge multiple players or armies working together. Defeat them using your armies to earn unique and valuable rewards.

Hunting uses Resolve (a special energy that regenerates over time or can be refreshed daily for a <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style> cost), <style="inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>, or a combination of both depending on the Encounter.

<style="Inline_Underline">You do not need tile adjacency</style> to attack. Unlike normal tile Defenders, defeating them does not grant tile ownership, it just frees the tile for future use.

Group Encounters are tough, you may need to attack multiple times, or coordinate with allies to defeat them.¬¬¯¯SPWN_SAVAGEDRAGON_SENTINEL_ALPHA_DESC¬¬A towering bulwark of fire and resolve, this dragon commands the flow of battle. With restorative flame and force of will, it shields allies, strengthens their strikes, and bends the fight to its design.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Hunt: Event Encounters</style>
<style="Inline_Bold">Encounters</style> are powerful enemies that appear on the map for a limited time. Defeat them with your armies to earn valuable rewards.

Hunting uses <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> (a special energy that regenerates over time or can be refreshed daily for a <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style> cost), <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>, or a combination of both depending on the type of Encounter.

<style="Inline_Underline">You do not need tile adjacency</style> to attack. Unlike normal tile Defenders, defeating them does not grant tile ownership, it just frees the tile for future use.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn Event Points:</style>

1. Find <style="Inline_Bold">Harren's Fallen</style> Encounters on the map.
2. Use <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> to hunt and successfully defeat them.
3. <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> regenerates over time or can be refreshed 3x daily with <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style>.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn Leaderboard Points:</style>

1. Defeat <style="Inline_Bold">Defenders</style> within any <style="Inline_Bold">Harren's Fallen</style> Encounter.
2. Each <style="Inline_Bold">Harren's Fallen</style> contains Defenders that must be overcome to claim victory.
3. Higher-level Encounters contain stronger and more numerous Defenders.

<style="Inline_H1">Alliance Ownership</style>
<indent=3%>- When your Alliance conquers a Harbor, all members can use and defend it.</indent>
<indent=3%>- To move through a Harbor, your Alliance must control both sides of the crossing.</indent>

<style="Inline_H1">Conquering Harbors</style>
1. <style="Inline_Bold">Coordinate</style> with allies
2. <style="Inline_Bold">Defeat</style> the Tile Defenders

<style="Inline_Bold">What are Star Up Offers?</style>  
Star Up Offers instantly grant all Dragon Relics needed to raise your dragon’s Star Rank. Each purchase unlocks the next Star Rank offer, continuing until your dragon reaches adult form.

<style="Inline_Bold">Why increase Star Rank?</style>  
Each Star Rank makes your dragon more powerful by:
• Increasing stats
• Unlocking new Habits
• Expanding army size
• Changing dragon size and appearance

<style="Inline_Positive">Star Rank progress never expires. Your dragon’s growth is permanent across Reigns.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Projects</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Tap to open the full <style="Inline_Bold">Barracks</style> or <style="Inline_Bold">Upgrades</style> screens, and keep both queues active to grow faster.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Upgrade Categories</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Upgrades are grouped into three categories:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Infrastructure</style> – Improves your economy and building strength.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">War Tactics</style> – Enhances your combat and troop effectiveness.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Care</style> – Boosts your dragons’ power and abilities.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Tap any Upgrade to learn more about its effect, cost, and requirements. Upgrades are divided into <style="Inline_Bold">Levels</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">Tiers</style>:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• Levels increase the power of individual buildings or abilities.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Tiers unlock new sets of upgrades once your Stronghold reaches the required tier.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Completing upgrades improves your <style="Inline_Bold">armies, economy, and dragons</style>, making them essential for long‑term success.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_BUILDER_TITLE¬¬Armies¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_SELECTION_TITLE¬¬Army Builder¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_GARRISONS_TITLE¬¬Garrisons¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_TILE_DEFENDERS_TITLE¬¬Tile Defenders¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_SIEGE_TITLE¬¬Siege Combat¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_BATTLE_REPORTS_TITLE¬¬Battle Reports¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ENCOUNTERS_TITLE¬¬Encounters¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_WORLD_MAP_TITLE¬¬The World Map¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_REGIONS_TITLE¬¬Regions¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_TERRITORY_MANAGEMENT_TITLE¬¬Territory Management¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_PIT_TITLE¬¬Dragon Pit¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_FEEDING_TITLE¬¬Dragon Feeding¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_HATCHERY_TITLE¬¬Hatchery¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_FACTIONS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">Being a part of a <style="Inline_Bold">Faction</style> gives you benefits including shared progress in some <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_events_1"><color=#36A0FF>Events</color></link></style></style>, <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_campaign_goals_1"><color=#36A0FF>Campaign Goal</color></link></style></style> progress and rewards, and being a part of new storylines from the world of Westeros and the powerful families of <style="Inline_Bold">Game of Thrones</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">You will be led by a <style="Inline_Bold">Faction Leader</style>, an iconic character and power broker in the world of Westeros, who will direct you to the most important objectives you and your allies should be focusing on.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Before your first <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_reigns_1"><color=#36A0FF>Reign</color></link></style></style>, you will join a Faction. This is in order to keep each Campaign fair and balanced, while giving as many players and alliances their indicated choice.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Together, you and your Faction become a part of the histories of Westeros and the wars fought over<style="Inline_SOP_Level_05">King's Landing</style> and the <style="Inline_Bold">Iron Throne</style>.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_CAMPAIGN_GOALS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_H1">Campaign Goals and Rewards</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each <style="Inline_Bold">Campaign</style> offers long-term goals that must be completed before the Campaign ends in order to earn powerful <style="Inline_Bold">rewards that persist across Reigns</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Faction Goals</style> – Team up with regional allies to capture <style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> and complete large-scale tasks for top rewards.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Personal Goals</style> – Earn rewards by tracking your own progress across the Reign.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• You must reach <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> Tier 10 before the Reign ends in order to claim rewards from Faction or Personal Campaign Goals.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Note</style> that Campaign Goal rewards are only <style="Inline_Bold">claimable at the beginning</style> of the next Reign.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Campaign Stages</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Campaigns</style> unfold in timed stages, each with objectives, effects, rewards, and story moments.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Stage Objectives</style> – New Faction & Personal objectives each stage.</style>
<style="Inline_Body"> • Some Objectives can <style="Inline_Bold">only be completed while in an <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_alliances_1"><color=#36A0FF>Alliance</color></link></style></style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Rewards</style> – Earned by completing objectives before the stage timer ends.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Stage Effects</style> – Realm modifiers (e.g., shorter <style="Inline_Stalemate">Stalemates</style>, more <style="Inline_Tile_Cap">Tile Capacity</style>).</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Story</style> – A scene unlocks at the end of each stage, reflecting your role and performance in matters of the realm as the Targaryen conflict escalates.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_EVENTS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Events</style> are <style="Inline_Bold">limited-time challenges</style> where you complete objectives to earn points and unlock rewards. Some events track only your progress, while others are Faction-wide and require teamwork.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style=Inline_Bold">Personal</style> – Objectives that you can complete solo, earning points toward milestones.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style=Inline_Bold">Faction</style> – Objectives where your Faction shares progress in points and milestones.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style=Inline_Bold">Global</style> – Objectives where the World shares progress in points and milestones.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style=Inline_Bold">Ranked</style> – Higher placement on the Leaderboard will grant better rewards for you, your Alliance, or your Faction’s performance.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Control Objectives</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Control</style> is a type of Event objective where Factions compete to hold key locations of Westeros. The longer your Faction controls these locations, the more <style="Inline_Bold">Control Points</style> you earn over time. These points help your Faction reach shared milestones to earn limited-time rewards.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">During a Control event, certain tiles become <style="Inline_Bold">active objectives</style>. Eligible tiles are highlighted on the World Map, and the event panel will direct you to tiles that are actively awarding points. Targeted locations may include:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">•<style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">•<style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> or <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Special Resource Tiles</color></style></style>

<style="Inline_Body">As your Faction reaches milestones, <style="Inline_Bold">every member</style> receives rewards that must be claimed. Early milestones are easy to reach, while later ones require coordination and a strategy for Tile Map control.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_QUESTS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">Chapter Quests guide your progress and prepare you for the final battle at <style="Inline_SOP_Level_05">King’s Landing</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Completing Chapters grants rewards like <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Relics</style>, <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style>, <style="Inline_Bold">Resources</style>, <style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Renown">Territory Influence</style></style>, and more.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each Chapter also reveals new storylines inside your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>, drawing you deeper into the world of Westeros as you advance.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_TERRITORY_INFLUENCE_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Title">Territory Influence</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Stronghold Tiers</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold Tier</style> determines what upgrades are available.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each new <style="Inline_Bold">Tier</style> unlocks an entire set of upgrades across <style="Inline_Bold">Infrastructure</style>, <style="Inline_Bold">War Tactics</style>, and <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Care</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Visually, your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> grows more impressive with each <style="Inline_Bold">Tier</style>, showing your rising status in the realm.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Reaching new <style="Inline_Bold">Tiers</style> is a major milestone, opening access to stronger abilities.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Relocation</style>

<style="Inline_Body">You can move your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> to a new tile using <sprite name="InlineSprite_Relocate"><b><#ddb673>Relocate</color></b>. This lets you escape danger, reposition strategically, or recover after defeat.</style>

You may only <sprite name="InlineSprite_Relocate"><b><#ddb673>Relocate</color></b> to a <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_regions_1"><color=#36A0FF>Region</color></link></style></style> where your Faction controls the <style="Inline_SOP">Seat of Power</style>.

<style="Inline_Body">• Any <style="Inline_Bold">in‑progress marches are recalled</style> to your new location.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• All armies stationed at your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> move with it.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• You cannot <sprite name="InlineSprite_Relocate"><b><#ddb673>Relocate</color></b> again until the cooldown ends.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Standard Relocation</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Standard <sprite name="InlineSprite_Relocate"><b><#ddb673>Relocate</color></b></style> moves your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> and armies to the tile you choose. If enemies capture it during the move or if you cancel, relocation fails — but no cooldown is used, so you can try again.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Standing Ally armies can never block your destination, but enemy armies can.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Quick Relocation</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><sprite name="InlineSprite_Relocate_Quick"><b><#ddb673>Quick Relocate</color></b> works like Standard, but the relocation completes faster and has a separate cooldown.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_STRONGHOLD_PVP_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_H1">Stronghold Defense</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> is your seat of power on the map. It houses your armies and dragons, but it can also be targeted by enemy players — defending it is vital to your survival.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Stronghold Durability</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> has a <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> stat, just like <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_points_of_interest_1"><color=#36A0FF>Points of Interest</color></link></style></style>. Each enemy <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege Attack</style> reduces its <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Forced Relocation</style> occurs if your <style="Inline_Bold">Stronghold’s Durability reaches 0</style> from enemy attacks — you will automatically be moved to a safer region.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">The enemy that deals the final blow will <style="Inline_Bold">steal some of your Basic Resources</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Attackers</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Enemy players can march directly on your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>. Successful attacks lower Durability and may result in lost resources.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Defenders</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Any armies stationed at your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> automatically defend it. In Combat, Defenders fight first before Attackers.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">If <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_alliances_1"><color=#36A0FF>Alliance</color></link></style></style> members have reinforced you, their armies defend before yours. Only if all defending armies are defeated does the attack deal <style="Inline_Siege_Damage">Siege Damage</style> to <style="Inline_Durability">Durability.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_BARRACKS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">The <style="Inline_Bold">Barracks</style> is where you train troops to strengthen your armies.</style>

They are helpful when preparing to siege <style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> or supporting deep pushes far from your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">How to Garrison</style>

<style="Inline_Body">1. <style="Inline_Bold">Conquer</style> any <style="Inline_Bold">Ruin, Town, or Castle</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">2. Tap the tile and select <style="Inline_Bold">Garrison</style> to assign an army to it.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Benefits</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Faster Marches</style> when armies are sent to a garrison.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Quicker Reinforcements</style> for stationed armies.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Recall Point:</style> Armies return to the garrison instead of your Stronghold when defeated or recalled.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Editing:</style> At garrisons you can <style="Inline_Bold">refill troops, adjust dragon lane assignments, or swap troop types</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Slots & Ownership</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each <style="Inline_Bold">Garrison</style> has limited slots for your armies. <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> and <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> unlock more slots at higher levels.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Map_Ruins">Ruins</style> unlock additional slots when you upgrade <style="Inline_Bold">Ruins Reinforcement</style> in <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_upgrades_1"><color=#36A0FF>Upgrades</color></link></style></style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> can only be conquered by an Alliance. If your Alliance owns one, all members can garrison armies there within the slot limit.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"> Same rules apply to <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style>, with the exception that they are Faction-owned, therefore only other Faction members can garrison their armies, march to or conquer adjacent tiles. ¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_COMBAT_OVERVIEW_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_H1">Combat</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Combat</style> is resolved through a maximum of <style="Inline_Bold">10 sequential rounds</style>. Victory is achieved when one side’s troops are reduced to 0.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each round, dragons act in order of <style="Inline_Dragon_Speed">Initiative</style>, attacking their opposing lane or using abilities like <style="Inline_Command">Commands</style> and <style="Inline_Habit">Habits</style> to shift the flow of battle.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">A lane is cleared when all enemy troops in it are defeated, allowing winning dragons to merge into an adjacent lane for a two-on-one advantage.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Visit your <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_battle_reports_1"><color=#36A0FF>Battle Reports</color></link></style></style> in your mailbox to see an example of how each element of combat plays out and works together.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Lanes</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Combat</style> is fought across three lanes: <style="Inline_LeftFlank">Left Flank</style>, <style="Inline_Vanguard">Vanguard</style>, and <style="Inline_RightFlank">Right Flank</style>. Each dragon leads troops in its assigned lane.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">A dragon must be in the <style="Inline_Vanguard">Vanguard</style> position for the army to be deployed.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Lane-Based Attacks</style> – Dragons primarily target enemies in the same lane.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Lane Defeat</style> – When all troops in a lane are defeated, the enemy can push through and threaten other lanes.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Lane Merger</style> – If a lane is cleared, surviving dragons may shift into neighboring lanes.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_TILE_DEFENDERS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">Every tile has two layers of defense: <style="Inline_Bold">Tile Defenders</style> and <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style>.

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Tile Defenders</style> are one or more armies stationed to protect the tile, and they must be defeated before any <style="Inline_Siege_Damage">Siege Damage</style> can be applied.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Durability</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> represents the strength of a tile’s fortifications. <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege Troops</style> deal the most damage to it.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Most resource tiles are unowned and have only a negligible amount, and can be taken without needing a full siege. In contrast, <style="Inline_Map_POI">Points of Interest</style> have much higher <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> and always require <style="Inline_Siege_Damage">Siege Damage</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">If <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> is reduced to zero, the tile can be conquered. If attackers fail to finish the job, <style="Inline_Bold">Tile Defenders</style> will return after a cooldown, restoring the tile’s protection.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Challenge Rating</style>

<style="Inline_Body">This is an estimate of how your armies’ power compares to the tile defending armies, and helps you decide what targets are feasible. <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_army_selection_1"><color=#36A0FF>Troop Type</color></link></style></style> and <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_army_selection_1"><color=#36A0FF>Dragon Affinity</color></link></style></style> are not included in the comparison—so synergizing these may allow you to overcome more difficult battles.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Note, <style="Inline_Bold">Challenge Rating</style> only applies to non-player enemies:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold"><color=#d92227>Impossible</color></style> – Opponent far stronger. Defeat is very likely.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold"><color=#e7903d>Challenging</color></style> – Opponent stronger. Expect heavy troop losses.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold"><color=#fcf069>Evenly Matched</color></style> – Armies are close in power. Outcome uncertain.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold"><color=#bed285>Favorable</color></style> – Opponent weaker. Victory is likely.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold"><color=#7eba98>Easy</color></style> – Opponent much weaker. Victory is very likely.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_SIEGE_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Siege combat</style> begins after all Defenders are defeated. Afterward, your army attacks the tile’s <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style>—deplete the tile’s Durability to conquer it.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Siege Damage</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Your army’s <style="Inline_Siege_Damage">Siege Damage</style> is displayed both in the March Screen and in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_army_selection_1"><color=#36A0FF>Army Builder</color></link></style></style>. This value is calculated from the combined siege strength of all three lanes.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Siege troops deal significantly more siege damage than other troop types, and pairing them with dragons that have positive <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_army_selection_1"><color=#36A0FF>Affinity</color></link></style></style> further increases their <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege Power</style>. <style="Inline_Map_POI">Points of Interest</style> have significant Durability and often require a Siege army to take over. A combat army can overcome the target’s <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> if it is significantly higher power.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Multiple Attacks</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Multiple attacks may be required to bring down the walls of tougher targets such as <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style>, <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style>, or <style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style>. Continue to send Siege attacks until the <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> is depleted. You have until the <style="Inline_Bold">Durability refresh timer</style> runs out to complete the assault and take the target. After the timer, all Durability will return.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Strategies</style>

<style="Inline_Body">To prepare effectively, it’s best to include at least one Siege-focused army in your roster. Using <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_garrisons_1"><color=#36A0FF>Garrisons</color></link></style></style> can help cycle these armies quickly and keep the pressure on. <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege Armies</style> will return to their previous position after an attack—make sure to attack from a tile near your target in order to apply multiple attacks in quick succession.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_BATTLE_REPORTS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_H1">Battle Reports</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Battle Reports</style> are sent to your <style="Inline_Bold">Mail</style> every time your army is in battle, whether you are the <style="Inline_Bold">attacker or the defender</style>. 

These reports help you understand how combat logic works and how your chosen army combinations perform together. Studying them can guide decisions about optimizing an army or identifying which enemy dragons that yours are strong or weak against. <style="Inline_Bold">Battle Reports are the best way to learn details about an enemy player’s army.</style></style>

<style="Inline_H1">What You’ll See</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Combat Summary</style> – High-level result (<style="Inline_Positive">Win</style>/<style="Inline_Negative">Loss</style>/<style="Inline_Stalemate">Stalemate</style>)</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Battle Logistics</style> – Battle location, comparison of army size, troop losses, and troop types.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Formation</style> – How your lanes lined up vs. the enemy.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Round Overview</style> – See which dragons and <style="Inline_Command">Commands</style> produced the most kills.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon XP</style> – Dragons earn <style="Inline_Buff">Experience</style> when enemy troops are killed, even on a loss.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Detailed Report</style> – Full breakdown if you want to study every action in each round.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ENCOUNTERS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Encounters</style> are special battles against non-player enemies that appear on the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_tile_map_1"><color=#36A0FF>Tile Map</color></link></style></style>. Defeating an <style="Inline_Bold">Encounter</style> grants <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_basic_resources_1"><color=#36A0FF>Basic Resources</color></link></style></style> or  <style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Meat"></style>Meat</style>, with chances for bonus rewards such as <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_special_resources_1"><color=#36A0FF>Dragon Relics</color></link></style></style>, <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_special_resources_1"><color=#36A0FF>Hatchery Keys</color></link></style></style>, and <style="Inline_Gold"><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_gold_1"><color=#36A0FF>Gold</color></link></style></style></style>. Higher-level Encounters yield better rewards.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Encounters consume <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style>, <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>, or sometimes a combination of both, depending on the type.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Unlike normal <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_tile_defenders_1"><color=#36A0FF>Tile Defenders</color></link></style></style>, <style="Inline_Bold">Encounters appear temporarily</style> and block the tile from being conquered until defeated.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Tile adjacency is not required</style> to attack an <style="Inline_Bold">Encounter</style>, allowing you to engage them anywhere they appear.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_WORLD_MAP_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">The <style="Inline_Bold">World Map</style> shows the entire realm and serves as the main tool for strategic coordination. Track <style="Inline_Bold">Faction control</style>, navigate to key regions, find <style="Inline_Bold">Points of Interest</style>, and share coordinates with <style="Inline_Bold">allies</style> to plan your next moves.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Faction Ownership & Colors</style>
Territory is color-coded based on which faction is holding that region. While faction identities may change across campaigns, these colors remain consistent:

<indent=3%><style="Inline_Bold"><color=#6CE2FF>Blue</color></style>
<style="Inline_Bold"><color=#FF5FF4>Pink</color></style>
<style="Inline_Bold"><color=#FFE731>Yellow</color></style></indent>

<style="Inline_H1">Points of Interest</style>
<style="Inline_Body">Special icons identify key <style="Inline_Bold">Points of Interest</style> on the map:</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Stronghold">Strongholds</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> (Level 1)</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Map_POI"> Castles</style> (Higher Levels)</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Seats of Power</style> display distinct levels:</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_SOP_Level_01">Level 1</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_SOP_Level_02">Level 2</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_SOP_Level_03">Level 3</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_SOP_Level_04">Level 4 (Capitals)</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_SOP_Level_05">Level 5 (King’s Landing)</style></style>

<style="Inline_H1">Coordinate Navigation</style>
<style="Inline_Body">Tap any location to view its <style="Inline_Bold">region</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">coordinates</style>. Share coordinates with your <style="Inline_Bold">allies</style> to:</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Launch synchronized <style="Inline_Bold">attacks</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Reinforce <style="Inline_Bold">positions</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Scout enemy tiles</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_REGIONS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">The realm is divided into many <style="Inline_Bold">Regions</style>, each with its own <style="Inline_Bold">geography</style>, <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_points_of_interest_1"><color=#36A0FF>Points of Interest</color></link></style></style>, and <style="Inline_Bold">strategic importance</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Region Ownership</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Regions</style> are controlled by the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_factions_1"><color=#36A0FF>Factions</color></link></style></style> that hold the <style="Inline_Bold">Seats of Power</style> within them.</style> <style="Inline_Body">Owning a <style="Inline_Bold">region</style> provides <style="Inline_Bold">strategic advantages</style>:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">   • Blocks enemy <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> relocations into the <style="Inline_Bold">region</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">   • Grants <style="Inline_Bold">defensive bonuses</style> to allied-owned <style="Inline_Bold">tiles</style> in the <style="Inline_Bold">region</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">   • Allows Faction allies to <sprite name="InlineSprite_Relocate"><b><#ddb673>Relocate</color></b> their <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_stronghold_overview_1"><color=#36A0FF>Stronghold</color></link></style></style> to valid tiles in the region.

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Region ownership</style> updates the coloration on the <style="Inline_Bold">World Map</style> as <style="Inline_Bold">Seats of Power</style> change hands.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_TERRITORY_MANAGEMENT_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">The <style="Inline_Bold">Territory Management Panel</style> lets you track and organize all the tiles you control.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Territory List</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Shows all your controlled tiles by type, level, and coordinates. Tap an entry to center the map on that tile. Filters and sorting help you manage large holdings.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Tile Capacity</style>

<style="Inline_Body">You can only control a limited number of tiles at a time.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• Gain +1 <style="Inline_Tile_Cap">Tile Cap</style> for every 100 <style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Renown">Territory Influence</style></style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Additional capacity may be unlocked through Chapter Quests and other rewards.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Abandon</style>

<style="Inline_Body">You can <style="Inline_AbandonTile">Abandon</style> tiles to free up tile capacity, making room for stronger or more strategically valuable ones.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">If you are at max <style="Inline_Tile_Cap">Tile Capacity</style>, you can still attack tiles, but you cannot conquer a new tile unless you abandon one first.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Where to Abandon</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Territory Management Panel</style> – Open your tile list and <style="Inline_AbandonTile">Abandon</style> directly from the entry.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• On the <style="Inline_Bold">Tile Map</style> – Tap any tile you control and choose <style="Inline_AbandonTile">Abandon</style> from the action menu.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Abandon Flow</style>

<style="Inline_Body">1. Select a tile you own (from the panel or directly on the map).</style>
<style="Inline_Body">2. Tap <style="Inline_AbandonTile">Abandon</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">3. Once confirmed, the tile enters a cooldown before reverting to unowned. During the cooldown, it still counts toward your <style="Inline_Tile_Cap">Tile Capacity</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">4. <style="Inline_H1">Dragon Collection</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Your collection includes all dragons you’ve unlocked, unhatched eggs you hold, and previews of future dragons to chase.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Every dragon you collect will be a certain <style="Inline_Bold">Breed</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">Rarity</style>. Breeds do not affect Troop Affinity.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Breeds</style>

<style="Inline_Body">A dragon’s Breed defines its combat role and style.</style>

<style="Inline_Breed_Champion">Champion</style> –  Champions weaken enemies or bolster allies, making them reliable core units in any team.</style>

<style="Inline_Breed_Hunter">Hunter</style> – Hunters excel at fire attacks and crippling debuffs that leave enemies vulnerable.</style>

<style="Inline_Breed_Sentinel">Sentinel</style> – Sentinels heal, buff, and control the battlefield, enabling allies to shine.</style>

<style="Inline_Breed_Warrior">Warrior</style> – Warriors smash foes with brute strength while amplifying allies’ damage.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Rarity</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Rarity determines how easy a dragon is to hatch and how many <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Relics</style> are needed to advance it. Rarity also affects a dragon’s starting stats—higher-rarity dragons begin stronger and scale better as they grow.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Rarity_Rare"><color=#36A0FF>Rare</color></style> – Common dragons, easiest to hatch, but modest starting stats.</style>
<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Rarity_Epic"><color=#E777FF>Epic</color></style> – Elusive dragons with strong starting stats.</style>
<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary"><color=#F0CA77>Legendary</color></style> – Dragons of legend, with incredible starting stats.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_FEEDING_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_H1">Feeding</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Feeding allows you to quickly level up your dragons using <style="Inline_Bold">Meat</style>. This lets you strengthen newly hatched or under-leveled dragons without consuming <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>, helping your whole collection stay competitive throughout the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_reigns_1"><color=#36A0FF>Reigns</color></link></style></style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Feeding and Campaign Stages</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• Each stage has a maximum feeding level your dragons can reach.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Dragons at or above the current <style="Inline_Bold">Stage Cap</style> cannot be fed further until the next stage begins.</style>

<style="Inline_H1"><style="Inline_Meat"></style>Meat Resource</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Meat"></style>Meat</style> can be earned as a reward from several sources including Quests, Events, Hunting Encounters, and the Market. It is only consumable during the current Reign. Any leftover Meat spoils and expires at the end of the Reign.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_HATCHERY_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Bold">The Hatchery</style> is where your dragon collection expands. By opening chests, you can obtain <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Relics</style>—the essential resource used to hatch new dragons and raise the <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp"><style="Inline_Bold">Star Rank</style></style> of dragons.

<style="Inline_H1">Dragon Relics</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Relics</style> will hatch the eggs of any dragons you've collected in the <link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_dragon_pit_1"></style><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><color=#36A0FF>Dragon Pit</color></style></style></link>. Acquiring additional Relics will increase the dragons' <link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_dragon_growth_1"><style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp"></style><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><color=#36A0FF>Star Rank</color></style></style></link>. There are three rarities of relics:

<style="Inline_Rarity_Rare">Rare</style>
<style="Inline_Rarity_Epic">Epic</style>
<style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary">Legendary</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Once you've acquired the maximum Rank for a dragon, any future relics of that dragon will convert to <link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_special_resources_1"></style><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><color=#36A0FF>Dragon Shards</color></style></style></link>, which can be exchanged in the market for <style="Inline_Bold">targeted Dragon Relics</style>.</style>

Half-swallowed by time, these sanctums still hum with power. Those who claim them harness <style="Inline_Curr_DurableUp_03">Dragonlord Scrolls</style>, a powerful currency used for Heirlooms.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Overview</style>
- Dragonlord Sanctums are found across the world, with <b>stronger</b> sanctums appearing in regions around King's Landing.
- Each sanctum is <b>player-owned</b> and continuously generates <style="Inline_Curr_DurableUp_03">Dragonlord Scrolls</style> while held.
- There is <b>no cap</b> on <style="Inline_Curr_DurableUp_03">Dragonlord Scroll</style> generation, <style="Inline_Positive">and any you earn are permanent and will not be lost upon Reign transition.</style>
- Sanctums are guarded by <b>multiple powerful armies</b>, and are more difficult than standard resource tiles.

<style="Inline_H1">Claiming a Sanctum</style>
- Sanctums have only 1 <style=Inline_Durability">Durability</style>—ownership is decided entirely through combat.
- Defeat the defenders to claim the sanctum before another player does.
- Once captured, generation details are shown in the <b>Rewards</b> section of the Tile panel.

<style="Inline_H1">Strategic Importance</style>
- Dragonlord Sanctums are <b>extremely limited</b> across the map.
- Control them early to deny powerful upgrades to your enemies.
- Expect fierce competition! Though Reigns come and go, Heirlooms carry their strength forward into every future campaign.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Overview</style>
• Heirlooms are a <b>permanent progression system</b> that strengthens your House across Reigns.
• Each Heirloom improves key areas such as <b>dragon power, economy, territory control,</b> and combat effectiveness.

<style="Inline_H1">House Level</style>
• Earn <b>House XP (Experience)</b> each Reign by completing Chapter Quests and Events.
• Increasing your <b>House Level</b> unlocks new <b>Upgrade Branches</b> and stronger upgrades within each Heirloom.
• <b>House Level</b> and <b>House XP</b> <style="Inline_Negative">reset at the end of a Reign</style>, but purchased Heirloom upgrades remain.

<style="Inline_H1">Heirloom Mastery</style>
• Each Heirloom grants a unique <b>Mastery bonus</b> that is always active.
• <b>Mastery</b> increases as you purchase more upgrades within that Heirloom.
• <b>Mastery</b> does not reset between Reigns.

<style="Inline_H1">Upgrades & Amplifiers</style>
• Each Heirloom contains upgrades arranged around a central <b>Amplifier</b>.
• The <b>Amplifier</b> strengthens all connected upgrades when activated.
• Purchase Upgrades using <style="Inline_Curr_DurableUp_01">Runic Fragments</style>, <style="Inline_Curr_DurableUp_02">Valyrian Tablets</style>, <style="Inline_Curr_DurableUp_03">Dragonlord Scrolls</style>, and <style="Inline_Curr_DurableUpgrades_Multiplier">Amplifier Seals</style> for Amplifiers.
• Upgrades can be <b>purchased before they are active</b>.
• Upgrades that require a higher <b>House Level</b> activate only after that level is reached.¬¬¯¯DIALOG_GOLD_CONVERSION_HEADER¬¬Spend Gold?¬¬¯¯DIALOG_GOLD_CONVERSION_BODY¬¬You do not have enough resources for this upgrade.

<style="Inline_H1">Hatchery Keys</style>

<style="Inline_Key_Premium">Keys</style> are used to unlock different chests for <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Relics</style> and other rewards.

<style="Inline_Key_Standard">Dragonbone Key</style> – Opens Standard Dragon Chests.
<style="Inline_Key_Event">Dragonglass Key</style> – Opens Event Dragon Chests with time-limited rewards.
<style="Inline_Key_Premium">Dragonfire Key</style> – Opens Premium Dragon Chests with high-value Relics and rewards.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>
• Complete <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_events_1"><color=#36A0FF>Events</color></link></style></style></color>, <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_campaign_goals_1"><color=#36A0FF>Stage Objectives</color></link></style></style></color>, and <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_quests_1"><color=#36A0FF>Chapter Quests</color></link></style></style></color>
• Defeat certain <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_encounters_1"><color=#36A0FF>Encounters</color></link></style></style></color>
• Some keys can be purchased with <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Dragon Relics</style>

<style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary">Dragon Relics</style> are used to hatch new dragons and increase their <style="Inline_Bold">Star Rank</style>. Different Relics are tied to specific dragons (e.g., Caraxes Relics).

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>
• Opening <style="Inline_Hatchery"><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_dragon_hatchery_1"><color=#36A0FF>Dragon Hatchery</color></link></style></style></color> chests</style>
• Complete <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_events_1"><color=#36A0FF>Events</color></link></style></style></color>, <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_campaign_goals_1"><color=#36A0FF>Stage Objectives</color></link></style></style></color>, and <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_quests_1"><color=#36A0FF>Chapter Quests</color></link></style></style></color>
• Defeat certain <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_encounters_1"><color=#36A0FF>Encounters</color></link></style></style></color>
• Purchase in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_market_1"><color=#36A0FF>Market</color></link></style></style></color>
• Purchase in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_store_1"><color=#36A0FF>Store</color></link></style></style></color>

<style="Inline_H1">Rarity Cores</style>

<style="Inline_RarityCore_Legendary">Rarity Cores</style> are used to upgrade the level of <style="Inline_Habit">Dragon Habits</style>.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>
• Complete <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_events_1"><color=#36A0FF>Events</color></link></style></style></color>
• Purchase in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_store_1"><color=#36A0FF>Store</color></link></style></style></color>
• Purchase in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_market_1"><color=#36A0FF>Market</color></link></style></style></color>

<style="Inline_H1">Relic Shards</style>

<style="InlineSprite_RelicDust">Relic Shards</style> are fragments from excess <style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary">Dragon Relics</style> of fully unlocked dragons. Trade them in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_market_1"><color=#36A0FF>Market</color></link></style></style></color> for targeted Relics or other valuable items.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>
• Collect <style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary">Dragon Relics</style> for a dragon that is already at maximum <style="Inline_Bold">Star Rank</style>
• Purchase in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_market_1"><color=#36A0FF>Market</color></link></style></style></color>

<style="Inline_H1">Breedmarks</style>

<style="Inline_Breedmark_Champion">Breed Marks</style> are used to upgrade the level of <style="Inline_Habit">Dragon Habits</style>.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>
• Defeating <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_encounters_1"><color=#36A0FF>Encounters</color></link></style></style></color>
• Opening <style="Inline_Hatchery"><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_dragon_hatchery_1"><color=#36A0FF>Dragon Hatchery</color></link></style></style></color> chests</style>
• Purchase in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_market_1"><color=#36A0FF>Market</color></link></style></style></color>

<style="Inline_H1">Campaign Favors</style>

<style="Inline_Campaign_Favors">Campaign Favors</style> are used to acquire unique items in the Campaign section of the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_market_1"><color=#36A0FF>Market</color></link></style></style>.

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>
• Complete objectives within <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_campaign_goals_1"><color=#36A0FF>Campaign Stages</color></link></style></style>
• Complete objectives within <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_campaign_goals_1"><color=#36A0FF>Campaign Goals</color></link></style></style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_BASIC_RESOURCES_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">Each of these <style="Inline_Bold">resources</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">currencies</style> expire at the end of each <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_reigns_1"><color=#36A0FF>Reign</color></link></style></style>.

<style="Inline_H1">Meat</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Meat">Meat</style> is used in <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_dragon_feeding_1"><color=#36A0FF>Dragon Feeding</color></link></style></style> to instantly grant <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Levels</style> without having to battle.</style>

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Purchase</style> in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_market_1"><color=#36A0FF>Market</color></link></style></style></style>

<style="Inline_Body">Newly unlocked dragons — <style="Inline_Bold">and all dragons at the start of a Reign</style> — begin with <style="Inline_Bold">bonus</style> <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each March costs <style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Stamina">10 Stamina</style></style> per dragon.</style>

<style="Inline_H2">How to Earn</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Stamina">10 Stamina</style> regenerates <style="Inline_Bold">every 45 minutes</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Resolve</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> is an account‑wide energy pool used to hunt <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_encounters_1"><color=#36A0FF>Encounters</color></link></style></style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Regenerates</style> over <style="Inline_Icon_Timer">Time</style>
