<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Purchase</style> in the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_store_1"><color=#36A0FF>Store</color></link></style></style></style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_FLYING_TITLE¬¬Dragon Flying¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_ACTIONS_TITLE¬¬Army Actions¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_ACTIONS_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_H1">Marching</style>

<style="Inline_Body">A <style="Inline_Bold">March</style> is how your army moves across the map. Marching lets you attack, conquer, reinforce, hunt, or move to a tile to defend it.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">1. Tap a tile and choose an action: Attack, Move, or Hunt.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">2. Select the army you want to send; the game defaults to the nearest available army.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">3. Review the costs (<style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> or <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style>), the march time, and the expected matchup if it’s an attack.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">4. Confirm the march. A banner marker will appear on the destination tile.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">March Costs</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> – Spent by dragons when marching, moving, or hunting certain Encounters.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> – Used instead of Stamina for certain Encounters.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Time</style> – March speed is set by your slowest dragon, with possible bonuses from <style="Inline_Habit">Habits</style> or upgrades.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Combat Outcomes</style>

<style="Inline_Body">When marching to attack a tile, results depend on battle performance:</style>
	
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Positive">Win</style> and break <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> <style="Inline_RightArrow"></style> conquer the tile.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Positive">Win</style> but fail to break Durability <style="Inline_RightArrow"></style> return to origin.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Negative">Lose</style> <style="Inline_RightArrow"></style> return to <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Stalemate">Stalemate</style> <style="Inline_RightArrow"></style> neither army is defeated after 10 rounds; the attacker regroups after a cooldown, and both armies remain on the tile during that time.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Reinforcement</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Reinforcing</style> adds more troops from your <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_barracks_1"><color=#36A0FF>Barracks</color></link></style></style> to an existing army. Reinforce after most battles to keep your army at top strength.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">You can reinforce armies at your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>, at a <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_garrisons_1"><color=#36A0FF>Garrison</color></link></style></style>, or directly to an army in the field. Reinforcements travel from your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> to your army.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Where to Reinforce</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• At <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> – Refill troops, change troop type, or swap dragons freely.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">At Garrisons</style> – Refill troops quickly, change troop types, adjust lanes; ideal for frontline support.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">In the Field</style> – Refill troops only; cannot change dragons or troop types.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Recall</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Recall orders your army to return from the field. Depending on where it is stationed, it will return to your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>, a <style="Inline_Bold">Garrison</style>, or its previous tile location.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Use Recall to regroup, edit armies, or pull them out of battle. Recalling does not consume <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Idle Armies</style> – Return to their <style="Inline_Bold">Garrison</style>, or to <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Marching Armies</style> – Can be canceled within a short window; they return to their origin, and part of the <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> cost is refunded.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Stalemate">Armies in Stalemate</style> – Retreat to their previous location.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Speed Ups</style> – <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style> can instantly complete a recall.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_MANAGEMENT_TITLE¬¬Army Management¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_MANAGEMENT_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body>Managing armies in Dragonfire requires strategy and balancing your dragons' <link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_energy_1">Stamina and Resolve</link> for maximum impact on the battlefield.</style>

<style="Inline_Body>You have a number of Army Slots available to you at the start of a Reign. As you upgrade your Stronghold, you will unlock more. 
<link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_army_builder_1">Build armies</link> with synergies of troops and Breed types within each Army Slot. You can save presets of army formations for future management of armies.</style>

<style="Inline_Body>As your primary army's Stamina is depleted, your secondary armies will have their Stamina to take advantage of. As you swap between armies, you can balance each individual dragon's Stamina to the fullest.</style>

Once your Stamina has depleted, use <link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_energy_1">Resolve</link> to take on Encounters and progress even further with your dragons!

<style="Inline_Body">Keep in mind, you can create armies <style="Inline_Bold">with less than three dragons</style>, and send them out for pathing and scouting, and reserve your best dragons for engaging in more challenging combat.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_COMBAT_OVERVIEW_TITLE¬¬Combat¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_PVP_TITLE¬¬Army PvP¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_ARMY_PVP_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">A <style="Inline_Bold">Player versus Player (PvP)</style> battle is initiated when two Player armies meet at a single tile on the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_tile_map_1"><color=#36A0FF>Tile Map</color></link></style></style>. PvP matchups are intense battles that may incur heavy losses on either side, so be sure to go in with your strongest armies to compete against other players.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Strategizing</style>

<style="Inline_Body">There can be <style="Inline_Bold">multiple Player armies defending a tile</style>, and each must be defeated to take ownership of the tile. You must defeat every player army on a tile in the order that they arrived—after you defeat the player army that is on a tile, you will then fight the <style="Inline_Tile_Cap">Tile Defenders</style> to fully conquer it.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Attacker</style> or <style="Inline_Bold">Defender</style> armies that lose their combat rounds will be removed from the tile and returned to their last Garrison point or Stronghold.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Just like standard combat at tiles, if after 10 rounds a victor is not decided, a <style="Inline_Stalemate">Stalemate</style> will occur. During <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_stalemates_1"><color=#36A0FF>Stalemates</color></link></style></style>, you may recall your armies to avoid additional losses.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Advanced Tactics</style>

<style="Inline_Body">It is recommended to <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_garrisons_1"><color=#36A0FF>Garrison</color></link></style></style> nearby a contested PvP area, as you may quickly reinforce your armies, wear down a strong enemy, or retreat to avoid being sent back to your Stronghold.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Habits & Lane Bonuses</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Where you choose to position a dragon can affect how some combat abilities perform:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Habit">Habits</style> – Trigger from any lane and may strengthen specific lanes regardless of position. When choosing lanes, consider your dragons’ Habits, which may have targeting requirements that impact your decision.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Breed-Based Habits</style> – At Level 16, all dragons grant <style="Inline_Buff">extra bonuses</style> only when placed in the <style="Inline_Vanguard">Vanguard</style>. They gain one buff themselves and apply another to either the <style="Inline_LeftFlank">Left Flank</style> or <style="Inline_RightFlank">Right Flank</style>. Since this is only active for the dragon in the Vanguard, consider which Breed-based Habit makes the most sense for your team.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Commands</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Command">Commands</style> will be triggered depending on their conditions. Some evolve as you gain levels and unlock new <style="Inline_Habit">Habits</style>. Be mindful of how a <style="Inline_Command">Command's</style> effects and how they pair with other dragons or counter your enemies’ dragons. Master all of your dragons' abilities, and they can be the difference in your battles against other players.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_TILE_MAP_TITLE¬¬The Tile Map¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_TILE_MAP_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body">The <style="Inline_Bold">Tile Map</style> is central to the gameplay of <style="Inline_Bold">conquests</style>, <style="Inline_Bold">sieges</style>, and <style="Inline_Bold">dragon warfare</style>. Armies move across <style="Inline_OwnedTile">Hex Tiles</style> to capture new territory. Each tile has a <style="Inline_Bold">type, level, ownership rule, and defenders</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Tile Types</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Resource Tiles</style>: Produce <style="Inline_Food"></style><style="Inline_Bold">Food</style>, <style="Inline_Wood"></style><style="Inline_Bold">Wood</style>, <style="Inline_Stone"></style><style="Inline_Bold">Stone</style>, or <style="Inline_Iron"></style><style="Inline_Bold">Iron</style> per hour, higher levels increase yield.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Encounters</style>: Defeating these grants <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_basic_resources_1"><color=#36A0FF>Basic Resources</color></link></style></style> and  <style="Inline_Meat"><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_dragon_feeding_1"><color=#36A0FF>Meat</color></link></style></style>, with chances for <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_special_resources_1"><color=#36A0FF>Special Resources</color></link></style></style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Points of Interest</style>: Provide strategic benefits such as <style="Inline_Bold">garrisoning armies</style> or <style="Inline_Bold">controlling regions</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Crossings</style>: Connect otherwise impassable terrain.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Tile Details</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Type</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">level</style> affect <style="Inline_Bold">resource yield</style> and the strength of  <style="Inline_TileDefender"></style><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_tile_defenders_1"><color=#36A0FF>Tile Defenders</color></link></style></style> and <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style>.</style>
• <style="Inline_Bold">Ownership</style> is indicated by <style="Inline_Bold">tile color</style>.
<br>You <b>can</b> conquer <style="Inline_RivalTile">Enemy</style> tiles by defeating all  <style="Inline_TileDefender">Tile Defenders</style>.

You <b>cannot</b> conquer <style="Inline_AllianceTile">Alliance</style> or <style="Inline_FactionTile">Faction</style> tiles.

<style="Inline_Body">• Capturing more <style="Inline_Bold">resource tiles</style> increases production.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Higher level tiles yield <style="Inline_Bold">more resources</style> but have <style="Inline_Bold">tougher defenders</style>.</style>

After you conquer a tile or <style="Inline_Map_POI">Point of Interest</style>, it will enter a <style="Inline_Protection">Protected</style> state for a certain amount of time. The tile cannot be taken by enemy players, providing you a strong but temporary <style="Inline_Bold">strategic advantage</style>. 

<style="Inline_Protection">Protected</style> tiles will remain safe while you continue to conquer additional tiles.¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_POINTS_OF_INTEREST_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Map_POI">Points of Interest</style> (POI) are key strategic locations across Westeros. They provide powerful benefits, enable deeper territorial control, and shape how Alliances and Factions expand across the map. Every POI comes with a <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_point_of_interest_bonuses_1"><color=#36A0FF>Point of Interest Bonuses</color></link></style></style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Seats of Power</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> (SOP) are major seats in Westeros, serving as centers of influence and control. Capitals are the highest‑level SOPs, representing seats of authority for the Great Houses. They are owned by Factions, and any member of a conquering Faction can move armies onto SOPs to defend them.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Capturing a Capital grants <style="Inline_Bold">Regional Control</style>, blocks enemy <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style> relocations, and provides defensive bonuses.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Regions and Capitals</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">The Crownlands</style> — King’s Landing, Dragonstone</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">The North</style> — Winterfell</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">The Vale</style> — The Eyrie</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">The Iron Islands</style> — Pyke</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">The Riverlands</style> — Riverrun, Harrenhal</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">The Westerlands</style> — Casterly Rock</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">The Reach</style> — Oldtown</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Dorne</style> — Sunspear</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Crossings</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Crossings</style> allow movement across terrain that would otherwise be impassable. They come in several types: <style="Inline_Crossing_Tunnel">Tunnels</style>,  <style="Inline_Crossing_Bridge">Bridges</style>, and  <style="Inline_Crossing_Dock">Docks</style>. 

<style="Inline_Body">To move armies through a  <style="Inline_Crossing_Tunnel">Tunnel</style> or  <style="Inline_Crossing_Dock">Dock</style>, your Alliance must control both end points.  <style="Inline_Crossing_Bridge">Bridges</style> only require one end point to conquer. Only Alliance members can stand on and defend the Crossing. Other Faction players cannot station armies there, but can occupy adjacent tiles — including the paired Crossing tile.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Garrisons</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Garrisons</style> are POIs where you can store your armies away from your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style>. You can edit <style="Inline_Bold">Troop Types</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">Lane</style> positions of dragons afield. Marches to, and reinforcements from, the Garrison move faster. It can act as a <style="Inline_Bold">Recall</style> point for armies. Ownership rules dictate how other players can interact with the POI tiles.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Ruins</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Map_Ruins">Ruins</style> are player‑owned forward bases ideal for exploration and staging attacks deep in the field. Only you can garrison armies in a Ruin you conquer. Alliance members can move onto the Ruin and defend it. Other Faction players cannot station armies there, but can occupy adjacent tiles.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Ruin capacity increases with the <style="Inline_Bold">Ruins Reinforcement</style> upgrade in your <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_upgrades_1"><color=#36A0FF>Stronghold Upgrades</color></link></style></style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Towns</style>

<style="Inline_Body">When your Alliance conquers a <style="Inline_Town">Town</style>, only Alliance members can move onto or garrison armies there. Other players in the Faction cannot station armies there, but can still occupy adjacent tiles.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Castles</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> are garrisons that offer a more fortified position than Towns. When your Faction conquers a Castle, only Faction members can move onto or garrison armies there, or occupy adjacent tiles.</style>
¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_POINTS_OF_INTEREST_TITLE¬¬Points of Interest¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_POINT_OF_INTEREST_PVP_TITLE¬¬Point of Interest PvP¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_POINT_OF_INTEREST_PVP_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Map_POI">Point of Interest PvP</style> is similar to standard <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_combat_overview_1"><color=#36A0FF>Combat</color></link></style></style>, with some additional rules and exceptions.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Faction‑owned Tiles</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Player armies may <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_garrisons_1"><color=#36A0FF>Garrison</color></link></style></style> at nearby locations and defend the tiles surrounding a POI. To conquer the POI, you will likely face resistance from these player armies.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">You must own an adjacent tile</style> in order to begin combat at a POI and remove the non‑player Tile Defender armies.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Combat</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Combat at POIs lasts 10 rounds</style>, just like standard Combat. If a <style="Inline_Stalemate">Stalemate</style> occurs, armies regroup as normal.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Conquering</style>

<style="Inline_Body">When Player armies are <style="Inline_Bold">standing on POI tiles</style>, their army — plus any Tile Defender armies — must be defeated in order to conquer the POI. <style="Inline_Bold">Player armies on a POI act before non‑player defenders</style>, with the last player army to arrive engaging first.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Once all armies are defeated, you may begin the <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege Combat</style> step. When POI <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> reaches 0, you or your allies will take control of the tiles based on the POI’s ownership rules:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> – Faction‑owned</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> – Alliance‑owned</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> – Alliance‑owned</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Map_Ruins">Ruins</style> – Player‑owned</style>
<style="Inline_Body">•  <style="Inline_Crossing_Bridge">Crossings</style> – Alliance‑owned</style>

After you capture a <style="Inline_Map_POI">Points of Interest</style>, it will enter a <style="Inline_Protection">Protected</style> state for a certain amount of time.¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_GROWTH_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_H1">Dragon Level</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Your <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Level</style> is your dragon’s seasonal progression. Dragons gain <style="Inline_Buff">Experience</style> (XP) from slaying enemy troops in combat or from being fed  <style="Inline_Meat"> Meat</style>. XP is earned in combat even when you lose the battle. Each level increases <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Stats</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">Troop Capacity</style>. Effectiveness scales with troop count and stats, with Dragon Level being one of the most powerful ways to improve both.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Dragon Stats</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each dragon specializes in different stats: <style="Inline_Dragon_Strength">Strength</style>, <style="Inline_Dragon_Intelligence">Intelligence</style>, <style="Inline_Dragon_Instinct">Instinct</style>, <style="Inline_Dragon_Speed">Initiative</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">Troop Capacity</style>. Pay attention to specific stats that may be best suited for particular dragons and their abilities. As a dragon increases in <style="Inline_Bold">Level</style>, higher stats improve combat efficacy.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Star Rank</style>

<style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp">Star Rank</style> represents a dragon’s permanent growth across every <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_reigns_1"><color=#36A0FF>Reigns</color></link></style></style>. Your dragons begin at <style="Inline_Bold">1 <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp"></style></style> when hatched. Collecting <style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary">Dragon Relics</style> for a hatched dragon raises its <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp">Star Rank</style>. From <style="Inline_Bold">2 <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp"></style></style> onward, each new Star boosts all of a dragon’s stats by a percentage, making them stronger and increasing their <style="Inline_Bold">Power</style>. As <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp">Star Rank</style> increases, dragons may grow larger in size and change in appearance.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Stars unlock your dragon’s long-term potential and are <style="Inline_Bold">permanent upgrades</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Breed Abilities</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Every dragon starts with a single <style="Inline_Bold">Breed Ability</style> that unlocks at <style="Inline_Bold">1 <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp"></style></style></style>. These abilities are unique to the dragon’s breed type.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Commands</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each dragon has a unique <style="Inline_Command">Command</style> that defines its core battlefield ability. They trigger when their conditions are met during combat. Some <style="Inline_Command">Commands</style> have an additional effect that has a chance to activate.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Habits</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Habit">Habits</style> are special passive abilities that define a dragon’s personality in combat. As a dragon gains <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp">Star Rank</style>, it unlocks additional Habits beyond its Breed Ability. 

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Habit">Habits</style> can be upgraded to improve their effects and are a major source of long-term dragon power. <style="Inline_Bold">2<style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp"></style>–10<style="Inline_DragonStar_Adult"></style></style> unlock Habits over time as the dragon advances in <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp">Star Rank</style>.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_DRAGON_GROWTH_TITLE¬¬Dragon Growth¬¬¯¯MINIGAME_DD_DEFEAT¬¬Defeat!¬¬¯¯MINIGAME_DD_PAUSE_TITLE¬¬Game Paused¬¬¯¯MINIGAME_DD_PAUSE_DESCRIPTION¬¬Defend the Stronghold against invasion by enemy forces.¬¬¯¯MINIGAME_DD_BUTTON_QUIT¬¬Quit¬¬¯¯MINIGAME_DD_WAVE_PROGRESS¬¬Wave {0} / {1}¬¬¯¯CHAPTERQUEST_CHAPTER_1_OBJECTIVE_2_TILEOCCUPY.LEVEL_CA_NAME_v2¬¬Conquer 1 Tile (Level 1+)¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_WHAT_TO_DO_FIRST_TITLE¬¬What to Do¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_WHAT_TO_DO_FIRST_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Bold">Dragonfire</style> is a game where you work with other players in your <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_factions_1"><color=#36A0FF>Faction</color></link></style></style></color> to capture key locations throughout Westeros. The ultimate goal is for your Faction to control <style="Inline_SOP_Level_05">King’s Landing</style> by the end of the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_reigns_1"><color=#36A0FF>Reign</color></link></style></style></color>.

To succeed in these long-term goals and win the best rewards along the way, you’ll need to work with your <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_alliances_1"><color=#36A0FF>Alliance</color></link></style></style></color> and Faction to complete time-limited <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_campaign_goals_1"><color=#36A0FF>Campaign Stage Objectives</color></link></style></style></color> while they are active. Consistently growing your personal combat and economic power is key to helping your team control the map. You should also explore the many types of <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_upgrades_1"><color=#36A0FF>Stronghold Upgrades</color></link></style></style></color> available, as their contribution to your combat power can be significant.

</style>
<style="Inline_H1">Phase 1: Plan the Attack</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• Choose a specific time to begin the attack together</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Conquer a tile adjacent to the <style="Inline_SOP">SOP</style> to enable the attack</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Decide how many armies each player will send, and what role they will play</style>

<style="Inline_Body">There are two army roles:</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Combat armies</style> to defeat the defending armies of the location</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege</style> armies</style> to reduce the structure’s <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">
If possible, choose dragons with <style="Inline_Bold">Siege Affinity</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Phase 2: Prepare and Position</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• Move your armies near the target ahead of time.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Account for march times so everyone arrives on schedule</style>.
<style="Inline_Body">• Moving armies nearby will require a friendly or <style="Inline_AllianceTile">Alliance Tiles</style> near the <style="Inline_SOP">SOP</style></style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Make sure your armies have enough <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> to fight</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Phase 3: Sustain the Attack</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Reinforce</style> your attacking armies as they take damage from Defenders</style>.
<style="Inline_Body">• Use <link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_garrisons_1"></style><color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><color=#36A0FF>Garrisons</color></style></style></link> whenever possible to reinforce faster</style>.
<style="Inline_Body">• Garrisons allow you to post armies closer to marching destinations that are far away from your <style="Inline_Stronghold">Stronghold</style></style>.
<style="Inline_Body">• Clear the defending armies before beginning <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege</style> attacks</style>.
<style="Inline_Body">• The Siege attack continues until all <style="Inline_Durability">Durability</style> is removed</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Capturing<style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> in the region also provides a combat bonus when attacking the SOP.

<style="Inline_H1">Other Points of Interest</style>
<style="Inline_Body">
Other locations like <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> and <style="Inline_Bold">Crossings</style> also require teamwork. These battles are smaller in scale but still require both combat and siege forces.

</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_MANAGING_DRAGON_ENERGY_TITLE¬¬Managing Dragon Stamina¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_MANAGING_DRAGON_ENERGY_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Managing your Dragon's energy</style> allows your dragons and their armies to take actions on the map, such as attacking enemy tiles or moving to a strategic location.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Each dragon in an army spends energy in the form of<style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> when taking an action. <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> generates over time, and there is no way to speed it up. This keeps all players on equal footing when it comes to how many actions their dragons can take.</style>

Dragons can also utilize <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> to spend as a resource that generates over time, or can be refreshed up to a daily limit <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> is used for <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_encounters_1"><color=#36A0FF>Encounters</color></link></style></style> and special actions on the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_tile_map_1"><color=#36A0FF>Tile Map</color></link></style></style>.

Balance your Dragon's <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_energy_1"><color=#36A0FF>Energy</color></link></style></style> on the battlefield to outmaneuver your enemies.

<style="Inline_H1">Managing Multiple Armies</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Dragonfire is a game about <style="Inline_Bold">managing multiple armies</style> at once. You can have up to 5 active armies, and using all 5 will help you achieve more across the map.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Using different armies for different roles helps you manage <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> wisely. Early in the game, this lets you save your strongest army’s stamina for the toughest enemies and most important battles.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">As you hatch more dragons over time and grow their power, you will likely <style="Inline_Bold">edit your armies to optimize</style> their power and try dragons in different roles. This is part of the fun of growing your power and becoming a fearsome icon in Westeros!</style>

<style="Inline_Body">Here are some typical army roles for you to consider:</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Main Army</style>

<style="Inline_Body">This might be your first, highest level, or highest Rarity army. You want the actions of these armies to have <style="Inline_Bold">maximum impact</style>. Let other armies pave the way for them so you can save your main army’s <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Pathing Army</style>

<style="Inline_Body">These armies will help you connect to higher-level tiles or important locations that you want to use your main army against. They usually capture weaker field tiles to create a path forward. Because these fights are easier, you don’t need to spend your strongest dragons’ <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>. You can even make an <style="Inline_Bold">army with one dragon</style> in it to take the most field tiles with this advanced pathing strategy.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Siege Army</style>

<style="Inline_Body">This army will be needed to take <style="Inline_Bold">Points of Interest</style> (POI) including <style="Inline_Map_Ruins">Ruins</style>, <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style>, <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style>, and <style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style>. Players in your Faction and Alliance will appreciate you building a strong <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege</style> army to contribute to team efforts.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">To create a <style="Inline_Bold">Siege Army</style>, change the troop type to <style="Inline_Troop_Siege">Siege</style> in the Army Builder. Pair with dragons that have <style="Inline_Bold">Siege Affinity</style>. <style="Inline_H1">How It Works</style>
- During a Control event, certain tiles become active objectives.
- Active Control Objectives are marked on the World Map and award event points while held.
- Progress is <b>shared across your entire Faction</b>.
- The longer your Faction holds an objective, the more points it earns over time.

<style="Inline_H1">Point Rate by Target</style>
- Level 1 Seats: +100
- Level 2 Seats: +125
- Level 3 Seats: +250
- Capitals (Level 4 Seats): +1,250

<style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Strike</style> brings your Dragonrider abilities directly to your enemies. Guide your dragon over the battlefield to defeat enemy armies and protect your territory.
</style>
<style="Inline_H1">How to Fly</style>

Steer your dragon by using <style="Inline_Bold">swipe controls</style>. Your dragon will change position with every gesture.

<style="Inline_Body">Your dragon breathes fire automatically at anything directly in its path. The <style="Inline_Bold">fire bar</style> shows your dragon's damage output. <style="Inline_Damage_Fire">Flame boosts</style> increase your fire’s damage.
</style>
<style="Inline_Body">Obstacles, ballistae, and enemy dragons can damage you–avoid these to prevent your dragon’s <style="Inline_Bold">health bar</style> from being depleted. Be on the lookout for <style="Inline_Recovery">Health boosts</style> to restore your dragon's health and outlast your enemies.
</style>
<style="Inline_H1">How to Win</style>
<style="Inline_Body">
Defeat the final challenge at the end of each run, and you'll earn a <style="Inline_DragonStar_Whelp">Star Rating</style> for how well you do. Replay levels to earn a higher Rating to get all possible rewards. Earn more points by defeating more enemies as you glide above the battlefield. New levels can be unlocked by meeting the level requirements.
</style>
<style="Inline_Body">Your choices shift the battle in real-time, Dragonrider. Launch a <style="Inline_Bold">Dragon Strike</style> to take the fight to the enemy and unleash the fury of your dragons from the skies!
</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_POINT_OF_INTEREST_BONUSES_TITLE¬¬Point of Interest Bonuses¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_POINT_OF_INTEREST_BONUSES_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style>, <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> and <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> give <style="Inline_Bold">Bonuses</style> to the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_factions_1"><color=#36A0FF>Factions</color></link></style></style> and <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_alliances_1"><color=#36A0FF>Alliances</color></link></style></style> that control them. These bonuses improve combat strength, dragon power, march speed, and resource generation, giving you and your allies the edge needed to claim key Points of Interest and Regions across Westeros.
</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Factions conquer <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> and <style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> to strengthen control of a region.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Alliances conquer <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> to expand reach and improve resource generation.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Starting Regions help your Faction build momentum towards <style="Inline_SOP_Level_05">King’s Landing</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• POIs in higher-level regions offer the strongest bonuses–but also the toughest fights!</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Regional Control</style>
<style="Inline_Body">
Regions become harder as you move from the starting regions up to the major Capitals of the Great Houses. The benefits and rewards also grow stronger.
</style>
<style="Inline_Body">Controlling lower-level <style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> helps your Faction conquer the next tier above it. As your Faction advances, you gain access to stronger bonuses and more valuable territory to defend.
</style>
	<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_SOP_Level_01">Level 1 Seats of Power</style> <style="Inline_Buff">grant bonuses</style> to conquer <style="Inline_Bold">Level 2 Regions</style>.</style>
	<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_SOP_Level_02">Level 2 Seats of Power</style> <style="Inline_Buff">grant bonuses</style> to conquer <style="Inline_Bold">Level 3 Regions</style>.</style>
	<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_SOP_Level_03">Level 3 Seats of Power</style> <style="Inline_Buff">grant bonuses</style> to conquer <style="Inline_Bold">Level 4 Capital Regions</style>.</style>
	<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_SOP_Level_04">Level 4 Capitals <style="Inline_Buff">grant bonuses</style> to conquer <style="Inline_Bold">the Crownlands</style> and <style="Inline_SOP_Level_05">King’s Landing</style>.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Evaluating POI Bonuses</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• Selecting a tile shows what bonuses a <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_points_of_interest_1"><color=#36A0FF>Point of Interest</color></link></style></style> provides when your allies control it.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• The <style="Inline_Bold">Army Select panel</style> highlights which bonuses are active for your March target.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• The <style="Inline_Bold">Boost Center</style> shows a list of all active bonuses and their conditions.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Seats of Power Bonuses</style>
<style="Inline_Body">
<style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> give stronger bonuses as your Faction captures more valuable territory, from minor keeps to the Capitals of the Great Houses.</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_SOP">Seats of Power</style> are controlled by your Faction and provide two kinds of bonuses:</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Local bonuses apply</style> to those in the region where the <style="Inline_SOP">Seat of Power</style> is located.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Cross‑regional bonuses</style> help your Faction push into tougher areas.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• <style="Inline_Bold">Combat bonuses</style> are granted for each Capital your Faction controls.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Castle Bonuses</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> are controlled by Factions and give bonuses against the <style="Inline_SOP">Seat of Power</style> in the region.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• These bonuses make it easier to attack that region's <style="Inline_SOP">Seat of Power</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Coordinate with your Faction to conquer all regional <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castles</style> before the <style="Inline_SOP">Seat of Power</style>.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Once a <style="Inline_Map_POI">Castle</style> is conquered, anyone in the same Faction can help defend or reinforce it.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Town Bonuses</style>

<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> are controlled by Alliances and increase resource generation for the entire Alliance.</style>

<style="Inline_Body">• Each <style="Inline_Town">Town</style> generates <style="Inline_Food">Food</style>, <style="Inline_Wood">Wood</style>, <style="Inline_Stone">Stone</style>, or <style="Inline_Iron">Iron</style> to all Alliance members.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Conquering <style="Inline_Town">Towns</style> helps Alliances grow stronger and expand across the map.</style>
<style="Inline_Body">• Once taken, all members of the conquering Alliance can garrison armies in the <style="Inline_Town">Town</style>.</style>¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_CATEGORY_ARMIES_TITLE¬¬Armies¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_CATEGORY_STRONGHOLD_TITLE¬¬Stronghold¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_CATEGORY_RESOURCES_TITLE¬¬Resources¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_CATEGORY_SOCIAL_TITLE¬¬Social¬¬¯¯CHAPTERQUEST_TILEOCCUPY.LEVEL_4+_QTY_8_EC_NAME¬¬Conquer 8 Tiles (Level 4+)¬¬¯¯NPE_SAGAMAP_NODE_1¬¬The royal egg was traced here.¬¬¯¯NPE_SAGAMAP_NODE_2¬¬Select the first encounter to begin.¬¬¯¯NPE_SAGAMAP_PLAY¬¬Tap to start flying!¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_HEIRLOOM_RESOURCES_TITLE¬¬Heirloom Resources¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_HEIRLOOM_RESOURCES_BODY¬¬<style="Inline_Body"><style="Inline_Bold">Heirloom Resources</style> are required to activate <style="Inline_Bold">Heirloom Bonuses</style>. <style="Inline_H1">Efficiency</style>

<style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Positive"><i>E</i></style></style> <style="Inline_Bold">Efficiency</style> determines the cost of resources, upgrades, and other actions in Dragonfire. For example:

	<style="Inline_Bold">New Cost</style> = (1000 / (1000 + <style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Positive"><i>E</i></style></style>)) * Original Cost

If you have +1000 <style="Inline_Bold"><style="Inline_Positive"><i>E</i></style></style> <style="Inline_Bold">Efficiency</style> to complete Stronghold projects, the time to finish the project is <style="Inline_Bold">decreased by half</style>.

Here is your prize for reaching #{0} on the leaderboard!¬¬¯¯UI_TILESELECT_GARRISON_TOOLTIP_TownPRG¬¬<style="Inline_Overview"><b>Towns</b> are strategic tiles that provide resource production for your alliance and act as garrison points once conquered.</style>

<style="Inline_H1">Alliance Ownership</style>
When your faction conquers a Town, all members can use and defend it.

<style="Inline_H1">Conquering Towns</style>
1. <style="Inline_Bold">Coordinate</style> with allies
2. <style="Inline_Bold">Defeat</style> the Tile Defenders
3. <style="Inline_Bold">Siege</style> until the Durability reaches 0
4. <style="Inline_Bold">Conquer</style> the tile

<style="Inline_H1">Garrison Benefits</style>
<style="Inline_Underline">Every alliance member</style> can garrison a limited number of armies in a Town.

<indent=3%>- <style="Inline_Positive">Faster Marches:</style> Armies march faster when sent to a garrison.</indent>
<indent=3%>- <style="Inline_Positive">Rapid Reinforcement:</style> Armies reinforce faster while at the garrison.</indent>
<indent=3%>- <style="Inline_Positive">Recall Point:</style> Defeated or recalled armies that are garrisoned return to the Town—not your stronghold.</indent>

At Towns, you can also change troop types and adjust dragon lane assignments in your army.

<style="Inline_H1">Managing Garrison Slots</style>
<indent=3%>- Garrison slots are limited by player.</indent>
<indent=3%>- To free up a slot, recall an army to your stronghold or station it elsewhere.</indent>¬¬¯¯UI_NODE_FINDER_NO_WEAKNESS¬¬No Weakness¬¬¯¯INFO_EVENT_LBONLY_ALLIANCE_PVE_CAMPALPHA¬¬Alliance: Defeat Tile <style="Inline_Troop_Shields">Defenders</style> and Encounter <style="Inline_Troop_Shields">Defenders</style>¬¬¯¯ACTIVITY_NAME_EVENT_LBONLY_ALLIANCE_PVE_CAMPALPHA¬¬Alliance Ranked: Crush the Defenders¬¬¯¯ACTIVITY_SPLASH_EVENT_LBONLY_ALLIANCE_PVE_CAMPALPHA¬¬The land bristles with shields and spears. <style="Inline_H2">How to Hunt: Event Encounters</style>
<style="Inline_Bold">Encounters</style> are powerful enemies that appear on the map for a limited time. Defeat them with your armies to earn valuable rewards.

Hunting uses <style="Inline_Resolve">Resolve</style> (a special energy that regenerates over time or can be refreshed daily for a <style="Inline_Gold">Gold</style> cost), <style="inline_Stamina">Stamina</style>, or a combination of both depending on the type of Encounter.

<style="Inline_Underline">You do not need tile adjacency</style> to attack. Unlike normal tile Defenders, defeating them does not grant tile ownership, it just frees the tile for future use.

Some Encounters may take multiple attacks—or armies—to defeat.¬¬¯¯CITYUPGRADE_CARTOGRAPHER_NAME¬¬Cartographer¬¬¯¯CITYUPGRADE_CARTOGRAPHER_DESCRIPTION¬¬Increases your <style="Inline_Tile_Cap">Tile Let us see which prove useful.¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_SKIRMISH_TITLE¬¬Skirmish¬¬¯¯INFO_GUIDE_PAGE_SKIRMISH_BODY¬¬A <style="Inline_Bold">Skirmish</style> is a type of march that allows you to fight  <style="Inline_TileDefender">Tile Defenders</style> repeatedly at tiles you already own. Skirmishing is a great way to quickly use your dragon's <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> to gain Experience (XP) for your dragons. You do not need to have available <style="Inline_Tile_Cap">Tile Capacity</style> to earn XP on the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_tile_map_1"><color=#36A0FF>Tile Map</color></link></style></style> this way.

To engage in a <style="Inline_Bold">Skirmish</style>, you must first unlock the <style="Inline_Bold">Skirmish Grounds</style> in <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_upgrades_1"><color=#36A0FF>Stronghold Upgrades</color></link></style></style>.

Once you've captured a <style="Inline_OwnedTile">Tile</style>, you may send <style="Inline_Bold">Skirmish</style> marches to rapidly convert <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> to XP. You can queue multiple Skirmish marches for each army, and there is no limit to how many armies can Skirmish on the same tile at once. 

<style="Inline_Bold">Skirmishes</style> work like normal <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_combat_overview_1"><color=#36A0FF>Combat</color></link></style></style> against  <style="Inline_TileDefender">Tile Defenders</style>: Higher-level tiles provide more XP but will incur greater troop loss, so be sure to look at the <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_tile_defenders_1"><color=#36A0FF>Challenge Rating</color></link></style></style> before committing your marches!

If you <style="Inline_Bold">Recall</style> an army during a queued <style="Inline_Bold">Skirmish</style>, all of its remaining queued marches will be canceled, and you will not spend the <style="Inline_Stamina">Stamina</style> for any marches that have not yet begun. There is a short timer in between each queued <style="Inline_Bold">Skirmish</style> to give you time to recall if you change your mind, or have taken more troop losses than expected.

Skirmishing is a great way to catch up during a <color=#36A0FF><style="Inline_Underline"></color><style="Inline_Bold"><link="deeplink:infoGuidePageLink:info_guide_page_reigns_1"><color=#36A0FF>Reign</color></link></style></style> and become an asset to your allies–and a threat to your enemies–on the front lines!¬¬¯¯EFFECT_NAME_CRESCENTBLADE¬¬Crescent Blade¬¬¯¯EFFECT_DETAILED_DESCRIPTION_CRESCENTBLADE¬¬After dealing <style="Inline_Damage_Tactical">Tactical</style> Damage, or applying <style="Inline_Recovery">Recovery</style> {ability=ability_command_legendary_crescentblade_wrxn_01:effect_group=1:trigger_chance} chance to grant Moondancer 1 stack of <style="Inline_Buff">Rising Tide</style> (Max 8 stacks). When an <style="Inline_Rarity_Epic">Epic Elite Drop</style> occurs, the chance of getting any <style="Inline_Rarity_Epic">Epic</style> Dragon Relic remains the same. When a <style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary">Legendary Elite Drop</style> occurs, the chance of getting any <style="Inline_Rarity_Legendary">Legendary</style> Dragon Relic remains the same.
